name: Cerulean sea
lede: Cerulean sea is a vivid greenish blue built on cerulean, the sky-blue pigment first sold under that name by the paint company Rowney in 1860.

sections.title: Sky-blue, named for the sea
sections.body: [[cerulean|Cerulean]] itself comes from the Latin *caelum*, sky, and Rowney began selling a cobalt-based cerulean blue paint under the name "coeruleum" around 1860, though Maerz and Paul trace an earlier recorded use to 1590 [1]. Cerulean sea pairs that pigment word with a landscape word, in the same descriptive pattern as many of our compound ocean and sky names [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 classifies it as a vivid greenish blue [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds Cerulean sea in 0.05 percent of its 23,781 paintings, 13 of them as photographed, rarer than 75 percent of the named colors we track [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 80 percent of its 5 clearest appearances [3]. The earliest match is a 1482 painting by [[painter:piero-di-cosimo|Piero di Cosimo]], well before Rowney's 1860 paint, as photographed, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. It belongs to the [[blue]] family, pulled toward green rather than toward violet, nearer [[sky-blue]] than any deep [[navy]] [2].
